input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent, not just okay. I don’t have Wi-Fi where I am, so I rely on my phone’s internet. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.
Yes, it’s happening on the phone with the number 555-123-2002. That’s the one I’m using right now, and the internet is just not working well at all.
I checked, and my phone shows a poor signal and says 2G at the top. I don’t see anything like Airplane Mode, Data Saver, or VPN—just the usual signal bars and battery. What should I do next?
Yes, I think I’ll need some help with that. I’m not very good with these settings, so step-by-step instructions would be great, please.
Okay, I changed the setting like you said. Now the top of my phone shows an excellent signal and says 5G. What should I do next?
I tried to check the internet speed, but it says there’s no connection, even though it shows 5G and excellent signal at the top. What should I do now?
I checked, and my mobile data is enabled, my SIM card is active, and I’m connected to 5G with excellent signal. I’m not on Wi-Fi or airplane mode. What should I try next?

I’ve reset the APN settings like you suggested. You mentioned I need to reboot my phone for the changes to take effect. I get a bit nervous about restarting—will I lose any of my photos or anything important if I do this?

I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t get any internet connection. The speed test still says there’s no connection, even though it shows 5G and excellent signal at the top. This is getting a bit frustrating—what else can we try? I really need excellent internet speed.

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent, not just okay. I don’t have Wi-Fi where I am, so I rely on my phone’s internet. Can you help me fix this?

To assist you with your mobile data issue, I’ll need to identify your account first. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID?

Once I have this information, I can check your line and help troubleshoot your mobile data problem.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

Yes, it’s happening on the phone with the number 555-123-2002. That’s the one I’m using right now, and the internet is just not working well at all.

Your line (555-123-2002) is on the Premium Plan, which includes 15GB of data per month. You’ve used about 8.7GB so far, so you haven’t reached your data limit yet.

To help diagnose and fix your slow or unreliable mobile data, could you please tell me:
- What type of signal or network (e.g., 5G, 4G, LTE, 3G) do you see on your phone’s status bar?
- Do you see any icons like Airplane Mode, Data Saver, or VPN?

If you’re not sure, I can guide you through checking these on your device. Would you like step-by-step instructions?
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
I checked, and my phone shows a poor signal and says 2G at the top. I don’t see anything like Airplane Mode, Data Saver, or VPN—just the usual signal bars and battery. What should I do next?

Thank you for checking. Since your phone is connected to a 2G network with poor signal, that’s likely the main reason your mobile data is slow or unreliable. 2G networks are very limited for internet use.

To improve your data speed, you should switch your phone’s network mode to prefer 4G or 5G (if available). Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to change your network mode to 4G/5G preferred?
Yes, I think I’ll need some help with that. I’m not very good with these settings, so step-by-step instructions would be great, please.

Here are step-by-step instructions to change your network mode to prefer 4G/5G:

1. Open the “Settings” app on your phone.
2. Tap on “Connections” or “Network & Internet” (the exact name may vary).
3. Select “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network.”
4. Look for an option called “Preferred network type” or “Network mode.”
5. Tap on it, and choose “4G/5G preferred” or “LTE/5G” (choose the highest available option).

After you make this change, your phone should try to connect to a faster network if one is available. 

Once you’ve done this, please check your status bar again and let me know if you see 4G, LTE, or 5G, and if your signal improves. If you need more help or the option isn’t there, let me know what you see on your screen.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I changed the setting like you said. Now the top of my phone shows an excellent signal and says 5G. What should I do next?

That’s great news! Now that your phone is showing an excellent signal and 5G, your mobile data should be much faster and more reliable.

Please try using your internet or any app that needs data to see if the speed and connection have improved. If you’re still experiencing issues or want to check your speed, I can guide you through running a speed test on your phone.

Would you like instructions on how to run a speed test, or is your mobile data working well now?
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried to check the internet speed, but it says there’s no connection, even though it shows 5G and excellent signal at the top. What should I do now?

Thank you for letting me know. Even though your phone shows 5G and excellent signal, if there’s no internet connection, there may be an issue with your mobile data settings or SIM card.

Let’s try the following steps to diagnose and fix the issue:

1. Check if mobile data is enabled in your phone’s settings.
2. Check if your SIM card is active and properly inserted.
3. Reset your APN (Access Point Name) settings to default.

Would you like step-by-step instructions for these, or do you want to start with checking if mobile data is enabled?

Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: active
Cellular Connection: connected
Cellular Signal: excellent
Cellular Network Type: 5G

I checked, and my mobile data is enabled, my SIM card is active, and I’m connected to 5G with excellent signal. I’m not on Wi-Fi or airplane mode. What should I try next?

Since your mobile data is enabled, your SIM card is active, and you have a strong 5G signal, the next step is to reset your APN (Access Point Name) settings to default. Incorrect APN settings can prevent your phone from connecting to the internet, even with a good signal.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings? After resetting, you’ll also need to reboot your device for the changes to take effect. Let me know if you’d like help with this process.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I’ve reset the APN settings like you suggested. You mentioned I need to reboot my phone for the changes to take effect. I get a bit nervous about restarting—will I lose any of my photos or anything important if I do this?

You will not lose any of your photos, contacts, or important data by simply rebooting (restarting) your phone. Rebooting just turns your phone off and back on, refreshing its system and connections. It’s a safe and common troubleshooting step.

Please go ahead and restart your phone now. Once it’s back on, try using your mobile data again and let me know if your internet connection is working. If you need help with how to reboot your device, let me know your phone model and I can guide you through it.

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Speed test failed: No Connection.

I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t get any internet connection. The speed test still says there’s no connection, even though it shows 5G and excellent signal at the top. This is getting a bit frustrating—what else can we try? I really need excellent internet speed.

Thank you for your patience and for following all the steps so far. Since you still have no internet connection despite a strong 5G signal, enabled mobile data, and correct APN settings, this may indicate a deeper technical issue with your line or device that cannot be resolved through standard troubleshooting.

I will transfer you to a human agent who can further investigate and resolve this issue for you.
